case_title: Pargan Singh v. State of Punjab
confession: Extra-judicial confession by appellants to PW-1, corroborated by eye-witnesses
aggravating_circumstances: Death of victim, serious injury to PW-2, traumatic experience for PW-2
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under sections 302, 307, 397 IPC read with Section 34 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that on 25.03.1999, two individuals on a scooter fired at the victim-deceased and snatched a money bag from him. When PW-2 tried to stop them, he was also shot. The assailants fled away. The victim-deceased was found dead at the scene, and PW-2 was injured. The police could not identify the culprits for several years until information led to the arrest of the two accused-appellants. The trial court convicted them under sections 302, 307, and 397 IPC read with Section 34 IPC. The High Court upheld the conviction. The accused were identified by eyewitnesses PW-2 and PW-3, who described the incident in detail. PW-2, the injured witness, testified that the accused shot the victim-deceased and then fired at him before fleeing. The incident lasted for 90 seconds, and PW-2 became unconscious after being shot. The medical evidence confirmed the injuries were caused by a firearm. The accused refused to participate in the identification parade, but the courts accepted the eyewitness accounts and the medical evidence as credible.
